summary: Replaced uncapped host-RAM reporting in all three current MPS paths with shared accounting based on torch.mps.recommended_max_memory(). Available memory is capped by both host availability and the remaining Metal working-set headroom after driver allocations. Older or failing PyTorch MPS APIs retain the prior host-memory fallback. Existing MLX serving code already sets mx.set_wired_limit() and independently budgets against max_recommended_working_set_size, so it was not duplicated.

tests.what_was_measured: 10 compatibility, regression, integration, system-pressure, and over-allocation tests covering the shared helper, SRT serving path, MPS device-property stub, and multimodal MPS platform.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, conflict, secret, and registered-test policy checks.

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned node is Linux/x86_64 and torch.backends.mps reports is_built=False and is_available=False. AMD GPU execution would not validate Apple Metal memory accounting, and this change has no numerical GPU kernel output requiring a ROCm reference.
remaining_limitations: No Apple Silicon/MPS device was available, so torch.mps.recommended_max_memory() was not compared directly with MTLDevice.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize on hardware.
No MPS model-loading or KV-cache serving workload was run; the regression tests exercise the same production call paths with deterministic memory API values.
Paging and machine-stability behavior cannot be safely qualified without Apple hardware under controlled memory pressure.

On older PyTorch builds where recommended_max_memory is missing, invalid, or raises an error, SGLang intentionally falls back to host memory reporting for compatibility and therefore cannot enforce the Metal guardrail.
No native rebuild was applicable because all changes are Python-only.
